A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AfriMed-QA study. Their main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite repagination.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM benchmark results and blinded clinician/consumer evaluations in Section 5, Figures 3–6, and the appendix tables.

after.justification: v4 retains those original evaluations and adds ROUGE-Lsum and QuestEval results for open-ended answers in Table 3.

M1.justification: Dataset construction, prompting templates, answer post-processing, and human-review procedures are retained. The additional evaluation metrics do not introduce a proposed algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same English AfriMed-QA MCQ, SAQ, and consumer-query coverage and retain the MedQA comparison. Dataset counts, countries, and specialties are unchanged; multilingual and multimodal extensions remain future work.

E2.justification: The evaluated model membership is retained across corresponding comparisons. Shortened OpenBioLLM, Llama, and PMC-Llama names match existing rows; ROUGE-Lsum and QuestEval are additional metrics, not new model baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 adds ROUGE-Lsum and QuestEval to the existing SAQ/CQ scoring protocol, retaining MCQ scoring, prompts, and human evaluation settings. Table 3 changes OpenBioLLM 8B/70B labels from Pretrained to Instruct, although v3 Table 14 already used Instruct names; different checkpoints or reruns are not established.

E4.justification: The explanation ablation, post-processing error analysis, geographic/specialty breakdowns, and human harm/omission analyses are retained. The added metric scores and discussion introduce no separate robustness experiment or metric-validation analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain mean ratings and confidence intervals in Figure 6. v4 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures; the new automatic metrics are reported as point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially expands open-ended results with SAQ/CQ ROUGE-Lsum and QuestEval measurements. Newly reported SAQ rankings place JSL MedLlama 8B highest on ROUGE-Lsum at 0.2758 and GPT-3.5 Turbo highest on QuestEval at 0.5072. Earlier accuracy, BERTScore, and human-evaluation values are retained; these are additional measurements, not same-metric performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The new metrics receive prose descriptions without new mathematical definitions, derivations, or formal properties.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the dataset novelty and scope, geographic/specialty performance variation, general-versus-biomedical model findings, and consumer preference claims.

C2.justification: New Sections 6.3 and 6.8 explain regional performance gaps through disease presentation and healthcare-resource differences, and discuss automated metrics' limitations. These extend existing interpretations without replacing the main conclusions. Some new metric generalizations are inconsistent with Table 3.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 clarifies the hardware description to specify one GPU of the listed types. New Section 8 documents consent forms, DUAs, privacy agreements, and the rationale for not requiring deidentification. Prompts, hyperparameters in Table 14, and dataset access/license information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds six references supporting the new metrics and their limitations, including Lin (2004), Scialom et al. (2021), and Hanna and Bojar (2021), and removes Chowdhery et al. (2023). The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds two discussion subsections and an Ethical Considerations section, expands Section 4.2, and updates contribution/affiliation notes. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains four metric columns, multiline headers, shortened labels, and an expanded caption. Table 1 wrapping and page layout also change. Existing figure artwork and the ordering of figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional scores and consent/privacy disclosure broaden evidence and transparency. However, new Section 6.8 says all BERTScores cluster at 0.86–0.89 despite retained SAQ values as low as 0.7938, and its broad QuestEval interpretation overlooks CQ scores clustered at 0.2336–0.2380. It also defers open-ended human evaluation despite retaining SAQ human results in Table 15. These inconsistencies weaken the main added interpretation, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
